mainTopic: Bird offerings: 'לא יבדיל' for a bird חטאת, squeezing blood of a bird עולה, and the new משנה on how place, method and intention affect bird חטאת and עולה
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's reading of 'לא יבדיל', said about a bird חטאת. The words mean the כהן does not have to separate the head, not that he is forbidden to. רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges this from the open pit, where 'ולא יכסנו' surely cannot mean covering is optional. The גמרא answers that the pit verse is followed by 'the owner of the pit shall pay', and that 'והקריבו' had already set the bird חטאת apart from the bird עולה. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a bird עולה is valid if the body's blood was squeezed out, but not if only the head's blood was. רבינא explains that this makes sense because most of the blood is in the body. Then פרק קדשי קדשים ends with הדרן. A new משנה lists when a bird חטאת and a bird עולה are valid or invalid, based on place (below or above the red line), method, and intention.

steps.title: Not separating is allowed, not required
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its reading of 'לא יבדיל': the כהן does not have to separate the head of a bird חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The words 'he shall not separate' mean] he does not have to separate it.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a statement that began just before this section. It says the verse 'לא יבדיל' means the כהן does not need to separate the bird's head from its body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have meant 'it is forbidden to separate.' The גמרא reads it more softly: separating is simply not required. This reading is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate (the bird's head fully from its body)
There is no need; it is not required
A bird sin offering

phrases.english: He does not have to separate [it].
phrases.notes: This explains the words 'לא יבדיל' (ויקרא 5:8), said about the head of a bird חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reading of 'לא יבדיל' begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא יבדיל' means separating the head of a bird חטאת is not required. It does not mean separating is forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge from the uncovered pit
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks: by that logic, would 'ולא יכסנו' about a pit mean a person does not have to cover his pit?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, said to רב אשי: If so, then about a pit, where it is written 'and does not cover it', would that also mean he does not have to cover it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא attacks the reading from Step 1. He uses a verse with the same kind of wording, where that reading would clearly be wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use 'ולא' plus a verb. If 'ולא יבדיל' only means 'no need to separate,' then 'ולא יכסנו' should only mean 'no need to cover.' That cannot be true, because a person who leaves a pit open is responsible for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a way to open a challenge by showing what an idea would lead to)
A pit, one of the main categories of damages
And he does not cover it
So too / would it also be the same?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
But if so,
regarding a pit, where it is written 'and does not cover it',
would it also mean that he does not have to cover it?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'לא יבדיל' means 'no need to separate'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same wording in the verse about a pit would then mean covering is optional, which is clearly false.

steps.title: The pit verse and the bird verse are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that for a pit, the next verse ('the owner of the pit shall pay') shows covering is required. For the bird, 'והקריבו' already set the חטאת apart from the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, since it is written 'the owner of the pit shall pay,' covering is placed on him. But here, since it is already written 'and he shall bring it,' the verse has already made a difference between a bird חטאת and a bird עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison. It shows that each verse has its own surroundings that decide how to read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the pit, the next פסוק makes the owner pay, so covering must be his duty. For the bird, the word 'והקריבו' ('it') said about the עולה already shows that full separation belongs only to the עולה. So we already know the חטאת is different, and this sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (pushing back on a comparison)
The owner of the pit shall pay
And he shall bring it (said about the bird עולה)
A bird burnt offering

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, since it is written 'the owner of the pit shall pay',
it is upon him that the duty to cover is placed.
But here, since it is written 'and he shall bring it',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:15. The word 'it' points to the עולה alone.

phrases.aramaic: חָלַק הַכָּתוּב בֵּין חַטַּאת הָעוֹף לְעוֹלַת הָעוֹף;
phrases.english: the verse has already distinguished between a bird sin offering and a bird burnt offering;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the pit.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases based on the surrounding verses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses use the same wording, so they should be read the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pit verse is shown to be a duty by 'the owner shall pay.' The bird verse comes after 'והקריבו' has already set the חטאת apart, so it can be read differently.

steps.title: Why 'לא יבדיל' is needed: no duty to separate
steps.stepSummary: Since the difference between the bird חטאת and the bird עולה is already known, 'לא יבדיל' must be teaching that separating is simply not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need 'he shall not separate'? Learn from it: he does not have to separate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It asks why the extra words are needed and returns to the conclusion from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'והקריבו' already shows the חטאת is unlike the עולה, 'לא יבדיל' seems extra. The גמרא uses this to confirm the soft reading: there is no requirement to separate, rather than a ban. The pit challenge is now answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking why words in a verse are needed)
Learn from it; conclude from this
He shall not separate

steps.whatToRemember: 'לא יבדיל' about a bird חטאת means the כהן does not have to separate the head. It does not mean he is forbidden to. The pit verse is different because 'the owner of the pit shall pay' makes covering a duty.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'he shall not separate'?
Learn from it: he does not have to separate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 3 and confirms Step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For a bird חטאת, separating the head is not required, and it is not forbidden.

steps.title: Squeezing only the body's blood is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's line about squeezing out the body's blood. It brings a ברייתא that learns from the word 'עולה' that this is valid even if the head's blood was not squeezed out.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] 'He squeezed out the blood of the body.' The רבנן taught: 'It is a burnt offering' teaches that it is valid even though he squeezed out the blood of the body and did not squeeze out the blood of the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא that gives the source for the משנה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that a bird עולה is valid if the body's blood was squeezed out, even without the head's blood. The ברייתא finds the source in the word 'עולה' in the פסוק. It shows that squeezing the body's blood alone is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He squeezed out (the blood onto the altar wall)
The blood of the body
The blood of the head

phrases.english: He squeezed out the blood of the body.
The Rabbis taught: 'It is a burnt offering' —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמִּיצָּה דַּם הַגּוּף
phrases.english: even though he squeezed out the blood of the body
and did not squeeze out the blood of the head [it is valid].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's ruling that squeezing only the body's blood is valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the word 'עולה' in ויקרא 1:17.

steps.title: Squeezing only the head's blood is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether squeezing only the head's blood is also valid. It answers no, learning from the word 'הוא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that if he squeezed out the blood of the head and not the blood of the body, it is also valid. The verse says 'it is' [to exclude this].
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake and then rules it out with a word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the head's blood is not required, one might guess the body's blood is not required either. The word 'הוא' limits validity to the case where the body's blood was squeezed out. So squeezing only the head's blood makes the offering פסול, as the משנה said.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a wrong idea that will be rejected)
The verse teaches (introduces the source that rejects it)
'It is', a limiting word in the verse

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird עולה, squeezing out the body's blood is necessary and enough. Squeezing out only the head's blood is not enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases: body's blood without the head's blood is valid; head's blood without the body's blood is פסול.

phrases.english: One might think: if he squeezed out the blood of the head
and did not squeeze out the blood of the body [it is also valid]?
The verse states: 'It is.'
phrases.notes: The word 'it' limits the rule: only squeezing the body's blood works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and rules out the opposite case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Squeezing out only the head's blood of a bird עולה does not make it valid. This is learned from 'הוא'.

steps.title: What is the source for the head-versus-body rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reasoning is behind the ברייתא's rule that squeezing only the head's blood is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the rule from the last step. This question sets up רבינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tied its rule to the word 'הוא'. That word alone does not explain why the body's blood counts and the head's blood does not. The גמרא wants to know what makes the body the part that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the derivation? What is the reasoning behind this?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the body's blood is enough but the head's blood alone is not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא's rule in Step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word 'הוא' points to the body's blood as the part that counts, and not the head's blood

steps.title: Most of the blood is in the body
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that it simply makes sense, because most of a bird's blood is found in its body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It stands to reason, because most of the blood is found in the body.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question with common-sense logic and not a new פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most of the blood is in the body, squeezing out the body's blood counts as doing the job. The head holds only a little blood, so squeezing only the head is not enough. This logic tells us how to read 'הוא'.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason; it makes sense
Most of the blood
Are found, are usually there

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird עולה, squeezing the body's blood is valid even without the head's blood. The head's blood alone is not valid, because most of the blood is in the body.

phrases.english: Ravina said: It stands to reason,
since most of the blood is found in the body.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule is based on logic. Most of the blood is in the body, so the body's blood is the part that counts.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק קדשי קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for פרק קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, קדשי קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך mark the end of a פרק and show love for the learning. A new פרק with a new משנה starts right after.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing line said at the end of a פרק.
The name of the פרק that is ending (the holiest sacrifices)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kodshei Kodashim

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last discussion

steps.title: A bird חטאת done the right way is valid
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens. A bird חטאת is valid when it is done below the red line, in the חטאת way, and for the sake of a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A bird חטאת that the כהן did below, in the way of a חטאת, for the sake of a חטאת, is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק begins with a משנה about the bird חטאת. It first describes the correct way to bring it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three things must line up: the place (below the red line on the מזבח), the method (the חטאת method), and the intention (for the sake of a חטאת). When all three are right, the sacrifice is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
A bird חטאת offering
Below, meaning below the red line around the middle of the מזבח
In the way of, using the method of
For the sake of, with the intention of

phrases.english: MISHNA: A bird sin offering that one performed below,
phrases.notes: 'Below' means under the red line around the middle of the מזבח, which is the right place for a bird חטאת.

phrases.english: in the manner of a sin offering, for the sake of a sin offering, is valid.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird חטאת done below the red line, with the חטאת method, and for the sake of a חטאת, is valid.

steps.title: When a bird חטאת becomes invalid
steps.stepSummary: If the method or the intention is changed to that of an עולה, the bird חטאת is invalid. If it is done above the red line, it is invalid no matter which method is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was done in the way of a חטאת for the sake of an עולה, or in the way of an עולה for the sake of a חטאת, or in the way of an עולה for the sake of an עולה, it is invalid. If he did it above, in the way of any of them, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the wrong ways of bringing a bird חטאת, and all of them make it invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below the red line, a wrong intention makes it invalid, a wrong method makes it invalid, and both wrong together make it invalid. Above the red line it is in the wrong place, so it is invalid whatever method is used.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering. Here it means a bird עולה, which has its own method.
Invalid, disqualified
Above the red line on the מזבח
All of them, meaning any of the methods

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a wrong intention alone is fine for a bird חטאת. The משנה says that even with the correct חטאת method, doing it for the sake of an עולה makes it invalid.

phrases.english: In the manner of a sin offering for the sake of a burnt offering,
in the manner of a burnt offering for the sake of a sin offering,
in the manner of a burnt offering for the sake of a burnt offering, it is invalid.
If one performed it above, in the manner of any of them, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists the invalid cases that contrast with the valid case in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird חטאת is invalid if it is brought for the sake of an עולה, or with the עולה method, or above the red line.

steps.title: A bird burnt offering done above the line in the burnt offering way is valid
steps.stepSummary: A bird עולה done above the red line in the עולה way is valid. If it was done for the sake of a חטאת, it is still valid, but it does not count for its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bird burnt offering that the כהן did above the red line: if he used the burnt offering method and had burnt offering intent, it is valid. If he used the burnt offering method but had sin offering intent, it is still valid, but it does not count for the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns from the bird חטאת to the bird עולה. It lists the cases where a bird עולה done in its proper place, above the line, comes out valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the place and the method are both correct, so the offering is valid. A wrong intention (for a חטאת) does not make it invalid. It only means the owner has not fulfilled his obligation. This is different from the bird חטאת in step 11, where a wrong intention made it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird burnt offering
Above (the red line on the מזבח)
In the way of, following the method of
For the sake of, with the intention of
It counted for its owner (fulfilled his obligation)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'valid' with 'counts for the owner.' In the case of a wrong intention, the offering is proper and is brought on the מזבח, but the owner still has to bring another עולה.

phrases.english: A bird burnt offering that he performed above:
phrases.notes: Above means above the red line around the מזבח, which is the proper place for a bird עולה.

phrases.english: in the manner of a burnt offering, for the sake of a burnt offering, it is valid.
in the manner of a burnt offering, for the sake of a sin offering, it is valid,
except that it does not count for its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the matching rule for the bird עולה, parallel to the bird חטאת rules in steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird עולה done above the line in the עולה way is valid. With חטאת intent it is valid but does not count for the owner.

steps.title: A bird burnt offering done in the sin offering way or below the line is invalid
steps.stepSummary: If a bird עולה is done in the חטאת way, it is invalid, whatever the intention. If it is done below the red line, it is invalid no matter which method is used.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he used the sin offering method, whether his intent was for a burnt offering or for a sin offering, it is invalid. If he did it below the red line, using the method of any of the offerings, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the bird עולה rules by listing the cases that make it invalid: the wrong method, or the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing the method to that of a חטאת makes a bird עולה invalid, even if the intention was correct. Doing it below the line is the wrong place, so no method can save it. This mirrors step 11, where the wrong place made the bird חטאת invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid, disqualified
Below (the red line on the מזבח)
All of them (any of the methods)

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird עולה: the place (above the line) and the method (the עולה way) are both required. A wrong intention alone does not make it invalid; it only stops it from counting for the owner. For a bird חטאת, by contrast, a wrong intention also makes it invalid.

phrases.english: in the manner of a sin offering, for the sake of a burnt offering,
or in the manner of a sin offering, for the sake of a sin offering, it is invalid.
If he performed it below:
in the manner of any of them, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the bird עולה rules by giving the invalid cases after the valid ones in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird עולה done in the חטאת way, or done below the line in any way, is invalid.
